packages.name: Block Ball
packages.summary: A brick breaker with power-ups, combos and five level patterns.
packages.description:
Break every brick with the ball and your paddle. Some bricks drop power-ups: a wide paddle, a slower ball or an extra life. Break bricks back to back without touching the paddle for a combo. From level 3 some bricks need two hits. Your best score is saved.

Mouse or Left/Right moves the paddle, Space launches, P pauses.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Block Drop
packages.summary: Falling blocks with a ghost piece, hold, combos and levels.
packages.description:
Seven pieces from a shuffled bag, a ghost showing where the piece lands, a hold slot and the next three pieces. Clear rows back to back for a combo; every ten lines it gets faster. Your best score is kept.

Left/Right move, Up rotates, Space drops, C holds, P pauses.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: SciCalc
packages.summary: A scientific calculator that shows the answer as you type.
packages.description: Powers, roots, logs, trigonometry in degrees or radians, factorials and percent, with the usual order of operations. The answer appears while you type; the history keeps your last 30 sums.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Vulkan Cube
packages.summary: Spinning 3D shapes drawn through Quin OS's Vulkan.
packages.description: A cube, a pyramid, a diamond and a prism, drawn with the same Vulkan calls a program makes anywhere: instance, device, swapchain, shaders, render pass, pipeline, command buffers. Drag to turn the shape; 1-4 pick the shape, C changes the colours.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Hello Terminal
packages.summary: A colourful tour of what the Quin terminal can draw. Run: hello-terminal
packages.description:
Rainbow text, a boxed table, a colour strip, a progress bar and a spinner, all with plain printf and escape codes. After installing, type hello-terminal in Terminal.

Commands:
hello-terminal  —  print the tour (colours, a table, a progress bar, a spinner)
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: cowsay
packages.summary: A cow (or Tux, a cat, a robot) says whatever you like. Run: cowsay hi
packages.description:
cowsay hello prints a speech bubble with a cow. -t makes it think, -f tux|cat|robot picks someone else. Pairs well with the fortune package: fortune | cowsay

Commands:
cowsay MESSAGE  —  the cow says it
cowsay -t MESSAGE  —  the cow thinks it (thought bubble)
cowsay -f COW MESSAGE  —  pick who speaks: cow, tux, cat or robot
cowsay -h  —  short help
fortune | cowsay  —  speak a message read from another command (reads standard input)
Long lines wrap at 40 columns inside the bubble.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: fortune
packages.summary: A random saying about code and making things. Run: fortune
packages.description:
Thirty short lines, one picked at random each time. fortune -a prints them all.

Commands:
fortune  —  print one saying, picked at random
fortune -a  —  print all of them
fortune | cowsay  —  have the cow say it (needs the cowsay package)
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: weather
packages.summary: Today's weather and a 3-day forecast, right in Terminal. Run: weather Tokyo
packages.description:
Type weather for where you are, or weather and any city, place or airport code. You get the temperature and what it feels like, wind, rain, humidity and UV now, then the low, high and what to expect for the next days -- with weather emoji and colours that follow the temperature.

weather -f shows Fahrenheit, weather -d 1 only today. Data from wttr.in (no account needed).

Commands:
weather  —  the weather where you are (found from your connection)
weather CITY  —  any city, place or airport code, e.g. weather Tokyo or weather JFK
weather -f CITY  —  temperatures in Fahrenheit
weather -d N CITY  —  show N days of forecast (1 to 3)
weather -h  —  short help
Data comes from wttr.in over HTTPS, so it needs a network connection.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: todo
packages.summary: A to-do list that lives in Terminal. Run: todo add water the plants
packages.description:
todo add puts something on the list, todo done 2 ticks it off, todo star 1 keeps it on top, todo edit, todo rm and todo clear tidy up. Plain todo shows the list: open things first, how long ago you added them, and what's done.

The list is kept in ~/.todo, a plain text file.

Commands:
todo  —  show the list (open items first, starred on top, then done)
todo add WORDS  —  add something (todo a WORDS works too)
todo done N [N...]  —  tick off one or more numbers
todo undo N  —  not done after all
todo star N  —  star or unstar (starred items stay on top)
todo edit N WORDS  —  change the text of item N
todo rm N [N...]  —  delete one or more items
todo clear  —  delete everything that is done
todo help  —  short help
The list lives in ~/.todo (plain text, one line per item).
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: pomo
packages.summary: A focus timer with a big countdown, a chime and a notification. Run: pomo
packages.description:
pomo starts 25 minutes of focus (pomo 50 for any length, pomo 25 write report with a label). A big countdown fills the Terminal with a progress bar; space pauses, + and - change it by a minute. When time is up you get a desktop notification and a soft chime, then pick a 5 or 15 minute break.

Every finished focus session counts as a tomato for today: pomo stats shows them.

Commands:
pomo  —  25 minutes of focus
pomo MINUTES  —  any length, e.g. pomo 50
pomo MINUTES LABEL  —  focus with a label, e.g. pomo 25 write report
pomo break  —  a 5 minute break (pomo long: 15 minutes)
pomo stats  —  how many focus sessions you finished today
pomo help  —  short help
While it runs: space pause / resume, + / - add or remove a minute, r restart, q quit.
When time is up: b starts a break, f another focus, q quits.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.summary: Slide the tiles, join equal numbers, reach 2048. Run: 2048
packages.description:
The classic puzzle in Terminal, in colour. Arrow keys (or WASD / hjkl) slide every tile; two equal tiles that meet join into their sum, and each move brings a new 2 or 4. Reach 2048 -- or keep going.

u undoes a move, n starts again, q quits. Your best score is kept.

Commands:
2048  —  play
arrow keys, W A S D or H J K L slide all tiles
u  —  undo the last move
n  —  new game
q  —  quit
2048 -h  —  short help
Your best score is kept in ~/.2048.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: matrix
packages.summary: Digital rain like the film, in any colour. Run: matrix
packages.description:
Green code rains down the Terminal until you press a key. matrix -c picks the colour (blue, red, purple, gold, white or rainbow), matrix -s 1 to 5 the speed, and matrix -m "WAKE UP NEO" has the rain leave a message in the middle of the screen.

Commands:
matrix  —  green rain until you press a key
matrix -c COLOR  —  blue, red, purple, gold, white or rainbow
matrix -s N  —  speed from 1 (slow) to 5 (fast)
matrix -m "TEXT"  —  the rain leaves a message in the middle of the screen
Options combine: matrix -c rainbow -s 4 -m "HELLO".
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: hexview
packages.summary: Browse any file as hex, with a text column and number inspector. Run: hexview FILE
packages.description:
Open any file and see its bytes: offsets down the side, hex in the middle, the text on the right, colour-coded so zeros, text, spaces, control and high bytes stand apart. Move with the arrows, jump with g (255, 0xff, +16), find text with / or hex bytes with x (89 50 4e 47), and n / N step through the matches. The bar at the bottom shows the byte under the cursor as a number (8, 16, 32 and 64 bit, little or big endian) and in binary.

It reads a screenful at a time, so even a huge file opens at once. hexview -d FILE prints instead of browsing (add -s offset and -n length), and some-command | hexview - reads a pipe. Remove it any time from the Package Manager or with: pkg remove hexview

Commands:
hexview FILE  —  browse FILE: offsets, hex bytes, text and a number inspector
hexview -d FILE  —  print instead of browsing (colour on a terminal, plain in a pipe)
hexview -d -s OFFSET -n LEN FILE  —  print LEN bytes starting at OFFSET (decimal or 0x hex)
hexview -w 8|16|32 FILE  —  bytes per row when printing
some-command | hexview -  —  read standard input (prints, does not browse)
hexview --help  —  short help
While browsing:
  arrows or h j k l  —  move the cursor one byte / one row
  PgUp PgDn or b space  —  move one page
  Home End or G  —  jump to the start / end of the file
  g  —  go to an offset: 255, 0xff, +16 or -0x10
  /  —  find text (n next match, N previous, wraps around)
  x  —  find hex bytes, e.g. 89 50 4e 47
  e  —  little / big endian numbers in the bottom bar
  w  —  bytes per row: auto, 8, 16, 32
  a  —  show or hide the text column
  ?  —  help          q or Esc    quit
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: musicviz
packages.summary: A live spectrum of the music playing, right in the Terminal. Run: musicviz
packages.description:
Start a song in the Music Player, open Terminal and run musicviz: a colourful spectrum (bass on the left, treble on the right) dances to the real audio. Bars rise quickly and fall slowly, with a little peak cap on each one, and only the cells that change are redrawn so it stays smooth. The top line shows the song, the artist and how far along it is.

It also controls the player: space pauses and plays, n and p (or the arrow keys) change track. m switches the look (bars, mirror, dots) and c the colours (rainbow, fire, ocean, mono). Start in a look with musicviz -s mirror -c fire. Remove it any time from the Package Manager or with: pkg remove musicviz

Commands:
musicviz  —  show the spectrum of the song playing in the Music Player
musicviz -s STYLE  —  start in a look: bars, mirror or dots
musicviz -c COLOR  —  start in a colour: rainbow, fire, ocean or mono
musicviz --help  —  short help
While it runs:
  space  —  play / pause the Music Player
  n or Right arrow  —  next track
  p or Left arrow  —  previous track
  m  —  change the look (bars, mirror, dots)
  c  —  change the colours
  + and -  —  more or less sensitivity
  q or Esc  —  quit
It needs the Music Player to have a song (start one there first).
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Quincraft
packages.summary: A complete voxel sandbox: endless worlds, caves, survival, crafting, mobs and day and night.
packages.description:
Build and survive in a world that never ends. Quincraft makes its own terrain from a seed: oceans and beaches, forests, deserts, snowy hills and mountains, with caves, lakes, lava and ores underground. Chop trees, dig, craft tools and armour, smelt ore in a furnace, farm wheat, and keep an eye on your health and hunger. When the sun goes down zombies, skeletons, creepers and spiders come out; by day pigs, cows, sheep and chickens wander the fields. Water and lava flow, sand falls, TNT explodes, and the weather changes. Choose Creative to fly and build with every block.

Worlds are saved in your home folder (quincraft) as you play. Everything -- textures, sounds, terrain -- is made by the game itself, so it needs no extra downloads. Remove it any time from the Package Manager.

Commands:
Controls
  W A S D  —  walk (double-tap W or hold Ctrl to sprint)
  Space  —  jump, swim up, fly up (Creative: double-tap Space to fly)
  Shift or X  —  sneak (won't fall off edges), fly down
  Mouse  —  look around
  Left button  —  hold to dig, click to hit mobs
  Right button  —  place a block, use doors/chests/furnaces/crafting tables, hold to eat food or draw a bow
  1 to 9 or mouse wheel  —  choose a hotbar slot
  E  —  inventory and 2x2 crafting (Creative: all blocks and items)
  Q  —  drop one item (Ctrl+Q the whole stack)
  `  —  show or hide the debug panel
  Esc  —  pause menu (options, save, quit to title)
Tips
  Punch trees for logs, make planks, a crafting table, then a wooden pickaxe. Furnace: 8 cobblestone in a ring.
  Torches (coal over a stick) light up caves and keep monsters away. Buckets pick up and place water or lava.
Options: render distance, field of view, mouse speed, volume, render quality, dynamic resolution and more.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: HD Audio Driver
packages.summary: Sound for computers with Intel High Definition Audio -- nearly every PC since 2005.
packages.description:
Quin OS has a built-in driver for the older AC97 sound chip. This driver adds the HD Audio controller that almost every desktop and laptop has instead (Intel, AMD and NVIDIA chipsets, and QEMU's intel-hda). Once installed, the Music player, videos, games and system sounds all play through it, and it starts with Quin OS every time.

It finds the codec's speaker, line-out and headphone outputs and plays through all of them, 16-bit stereo at 8 to 192 kHz, with volume control. Not supported yet: recording, HDMI and DisplayPort audio, and switching outputs when headphones are plugged in.

Terminal: lsmod shows it running, rmmod hda_audio stops it.
packages.author: Quin OS Team
